newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise no comment again on Suez.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise no comment again on Suez.

text.p: French water company Lyonnaise des Eaux declined all comment again on Friday on further reports that an agreement to merge with conglomerate Suez is close to being wrapped up, possibly as early as next Wednesday.
"Nothing at all," a Lyonnaise spokeswoman said when asked by Reuters to comment on Friday.

No one was immediately available at Suez for comment on fresh newspaper reports, including one in La Tribune business daily which said sources had confirmed merger talks had gone into the final phase and the main hurdles had been overcome.
The stock market has been alight for more than a week and betting on a deal. Analysts say it is a more a question of when and on what terms it will happen rather than if it will happen.

La Tribune said on Friday a string of merchant banks have been working all out on a merger for weeks and suggested it could take the form of a share exchange of two Suez shares for each Lyonnaise share accompanied by an exceptional dividend payment to win backing from Suez shareholders.
Both companies have repeately declined to comment, amid heavy trading in their shares. The French stock market was closed on Friday for the Easter holiday weekend and will also be closed on Monday.
Lyonnaise and Suez both have board meetings next week to approve 1996 results, with announcement of their annual figures respectively on Thursday and Wednesday.
